name: Unmarked Stratton 5-String Banjo
description: Superb condition, plays great. Features an 11-inch pot. A wonderful vintage instrument with excellent character and tone.

name: 1928 Gibson TB-3 Mastertone
description: Rare pre-war banjo, gold-plated hardware, original case included. Excellent condition.

name: 1956 Vega Vegaphone
description: Warm, rich tone. Fully restored and ready to play. Beautiful walnut neck.

name: 1890s S.S. Stewart Special
description: Museum piece. One of the finest banjos ever made. Not for sale — part of permanent collection.

name: R. J. Stratton Banjo
description: Very rare banjo. The actual body was produced by Buckbee's. Wonderful banjo, the sound is absolutely superb. A beautiful banjo to play.

name: Barnes & Mullins — Pre-Lyratone Open Back
description: 5-string open back banjo, pre-Lyratone era. Typical heavy construction synonymous with J.G. Abbott. Fitted with a pickup and produces an incredible tone.

name: Barnes & Mullins — Early Zither Banjo
description: Early Zither banjo around 1890. Features automatic mute controlled by a button on the rear of the pan — brings a platform up against the bridge for silent practice. Beautifully made and marked.

name: Barnes & Mullins — Pre-Sandringham Zither
description: Zither banjo from around 1910. More or less scrap when acquired, but fully restored with great care. Now plays with volume and wonderful tone.

name: Clifford Essex — Popular No.1
description: Lovely quality banjo. A fine example of Clifford Essex's entry-level but well-respected 'Popular' model range. Clean, clear tone and excellent playability.

name: Clifford Essex — Clipper
description: The Clipper model from Clifford Essex. A beautiful instrument with great character and tone. Well made and a pleasure to play.

name: Clifford Essex — Essex Cammeyer 5-String
description: Early 5-string banjo, probably an apprentice piece. Nice carved heel, mother-of-pearl inlays marking the frets and position markers. Marked 'X.V.' on the perch pole — a trade mark of Essex Cammeyer. Wonderful tone.

name: J. E. Dallas — 5-String Banjo
description: A 19th century banjo by one of London's finest makers. Another high-end five-string banjo which plays so beautifully. Has been used in recording work — just a real gem to play.

name: John Alvey Turner — 12-Inch Head Banjo
description: Another great quality banjo sold by the renowned London firm. The maker is unknown but it features a 12-inch head and is an absolute pleasure to play.

name: W. Temlett — Zither Banjo
description: Fine example by one of England's earliest and most important banjo makers. W. Temlett was making instruments in London from the mid-1800s. Beautifully made with the characteristic Temlett styling and tone.

name: Windsor — 5-String Banjo
description: Made by A. O. Windsor of Birmingham. High-quality British banjo with the characteristic Windsor construction and tone. Wonderful playing instrument.

name: Ajax by W. Temlett
description: A fine example of its type, crafted mainly from lovely rosewood. Truly a dream to play. Circa 1880.

name: George P. Matthews — Fretless Banjo
description: An early Matthews banjo, originally fretless with an 11-inch head and 30 clamps. Has a wonderful real antique sound.

name: George P. Matthews — 12¼-Inch Head Banjo
description: Features a large 12¼-inch head — superb for slide work. Beautiful tone and volume.

name: J.C. Bertolle — 'B & T' Dexter Model
description: A Dexter banjo made exclusively for J.C. Bertolle. Bears all the hallmarks of Richard Spencer craftsmanship. Three-piece neck with sculptured perch pole. Exquisite mother-of-pearl inlay with finest engraving even to the minutest detail. In 45 years of collecting, this is — in my opinion and many others — one of the finest English banjos ever made. The sound is outstanding, clear as a bell.

name: Leon Clerc — 5-String Banjo
description: Made by Leon Eugene Clerc of London. Banjos and zither-banjos carried the names 'Athena', 'Crescent' and 'Marvel'. Beautifully crafted instrument from one of London's respected 19th century makers.

name: Jimmy Parslow Banjo
description: A rare British banjo with a wonderfully sweet sound and plenty of volume. Beautifully restored and a welcome addition to the collection.

name: Crosby — F.C. Wilkes Banjo
description: A fine example of a Crosby banjo retailed by F.C. Wilkes. Circa 1900. Joseph Crosby was a rare and highly regarded English banjo maker — examples rarely come on the market. Beautifully made and a treasured part of the collection.

name: George Houghton — High-Grade 5-String
description: A lovely banjo in every respect. Made by George Houghton of Birmingham, a respected British maker of the early 20th century. Fully refurbished and now a wonderful instrument to play.

name: J.K. Simson Banjo
description: A fine British banjo by J.K. Simson. Well-crafted instrument from one of England's respected makers. Clean tone and excellent build quality.

name: Joe Daniel's 5-String Banjo
description: A British banjo bearing the name Joe Daniel's. Characterful instrument with plenty of volume and warmth. A fine example of British craftsmanship.

name: John Grey & Sons Banjo
description: Sold by the renowned London firm John Grey & Sons. Quality British banjo with excellent tone and construction.

name: Norton Greenopp Banjo
description: A rare and interesting British banjo. Norton Greenopp instruments are distinctive and highly collectable.

name: Peerless 5-String Banjo
description: British-made banjo under the 'Peerless' name. Excellent quality and playability — lives up to its name.

name: Lyon & Healy — British Market Model
description: Fine banjo retailed or made for the British market by the famous firm of Lyon & Healy. High-quality instrument with exceptional tone.

name: J.B. Schall Banjo
description: A rare British banjo by J.B. Schall. Beautifully crafted and a wonderful addition to the collection.

name: Sears Banjo
description: British-made banjo retailed under the Sears name. Solid, well-built instrument with good tone and playability.

name: Thompson and O'Dell Banjo
description: Fine banjo by the partnership of Thompson and O'Dell. Well-regarded British makers producing quality instruments.

name: T. Bostock Banjo
description: A rare 19th century British banjo by T. Bostock. Wonderful character and tone from this early maker.

name: T. Lyons Banjo
description: Fine British banjo from the maker T. Lyons. Beautifully constructed with warm, clear tone.
